body_markdown:
*Last updated: November 2026*


## Key takeaways


-


EPM software (enterprise performance management, also called CPM) sits on top of your ERP to plan, budget, forecast, control and analyze performance.


-


The four jobs to test are budgeting, planning, control and allocation. A platform that does one well and the others awkwardly leaves finance reconciling the gaps.


-


Compare platforms on approvals and audit trail, driver-based allocation, AI governance, integrations and who owns the model after go-live.


-


Spreadsheet-first teams should look first at a platform that keeps spreadsheet flexibility while removing spreadsheet limits.


## Introduction


The eight EPM platforms worth comparing for budgeting, planning, control and allocation in 2026 are Abacum, Workday Adaptive Planning, Anaplan, Oracle Cloud EPM Planning, OneStream, Planful, Pigment and Vena. They differ in how much they ask your team to build, how they handle approvals and how they bring AI into the work.


Abacum is the AI-native FP&A platform finance trusts, and the business planning platform the whole company runs on. It runs on one governed layer of data, logic and context: data is the what, logic is the how, context is the why.


If your question is "what software options exist for budgeting, planning, control and allocation," this guide gives you a structured answer: what EPM software is, how the platforms compare on the four jobs and how to choose without a months-long search.


## What is EPM software and how is it different from ERP?


EPM software helps organizations plan, budget, forecast and analyze financial and operational performance. ERP systems record transactions: payables, receivables, inventory and the general ledger. EPM sits on top of that data and turns it into plans, forecasts and decisions about what should happen next. For more on the distinction, see our guide to[EPM vs ERP](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/epm-vs-erp) and our[enterprise performance management overview](https://www.abacum.ai/blog/enterprise-performance-management) .


Most EPM platforms connect to your ERP, CRM and HR systems to pull actuals automatically, then support driver-based planning, rolling forecasts, scenario work, approvals and management reporting.


## The four jobs EPM software has to do


-


**Budgeting.** Budget owners build and submit plans, and finance approves them.


-


**Planning.** Forecasts and scenarios update as the business changes.


-


**Control.** Variance analysis, approvals and an audit trail keep the plan honest during the year.


-


**Allocation.** Shared costs and resources are distributed by drivers you can see and change.


## 8 EPM software platforms to consider


### 1. Abacum


**Best for:** Finance teams that want enterprise AI built in from day one, one plan the whole business runs on, and a model that finance owns.


We built Abacum as the AI-native business planning platform for scaling enterprises. It brings enterprise-grade depth with consumer-grade ease: governance, security and scale owned by finance and live in weeks, not quarters, guided by our in-house FP&A experts rather than third-party consultants.


On **budgeting and control** , budget owners work in dedicated Spaces with controlled access. Submissions move through statuses (in progress, submitted, approved), permissions change by stage, finance owns the approvals and the final number, and every change is tracked in an audit trail. On **allocation** , rules are driver-based, so $600K of shared IT cost allocated by headcount across departments of 50, 30 and 20 people becomes $300K, $180K and $120K and updates automatically when headcount changes. On **planning** , Abacum plans, forecasts and reports at weekly granularity, so you can reforecast whenever the business shifts and answer the board's question the same day it is asked.


AI Modeler changes who can keep a model current. Describe what you need in plain language, or start from the spreadsheet you already built, and get a working model in minutes. ### 2. Workday Adaptive Planning


**Best for:** Teams already on Workday that want workforce and financial planning on one connected platform.


Workday Adaptive Planning is a cloud-based FP&A platform with particular depth in workforce planning and native integration with Workday HCM and Workday Financials. For organizations running payroll and HR on Workday, actuals flow through without a separate integration build. It supports rolling forecasts, scenario modeling and collaborative budgeting with a structured approval layer. Teams outside Workday can use pre-built connectors and APIs, though the native advantage is largest for existing Workday customers.


### 3. Anaplan


**Best for:** Planning programs with dedicated model builders.


Anaplan is a long-standing connected planning platform with multi-dimensional modeling, a large template ecosystem and connections to major ERP and CRM systems. It supports intricate model designs and large data volumes. The depth comes with a steeper setup and administration curve, so confirm who will build and maintain the model after go-live.


### 4. Oracle Cloud EPM Planning


**Best for:** Organizations invested in the Oracle ecosystem that want module-based planning.


Oracle's documentation describes module-based planning for Financials, Workforce, Capital, Projects and Strategic Modeling, with predefined forms, calculations, dashboards and drivers in each module. Review which modules you would enable and what configuration each requires.


### 5. OneStream


**Best for:** Teams that want planning, financial close and reporting on one platform.


OneStream describes itself as a unified platform for financial close, planning, reporting and operational data, and says teams can start with a single capability and add others later. It positions itself alongside your ERP rather than as a replacement. It also says models, workflows and dashboards are controlled by finance. Confirm the scope of the first phase and the effort to reach it.


### 6. Planful


**Best for:** Finance teams that want a structured, process-driven platform covering budgeting, close and reporting.


Planful is a cloud-based corporate performance management platform with modules for budgeting, financial close and reporting. It supports multi-entity roll-ups and structured planning cycles, and offers an Excel add-in for teams that prefer spreadsheet input. Implementation involves structured configuration work and benefits from defined internal ownership.


### 7. Pigment


**Best for:** Teams willing to build and maintain their own planning models in a flexible modeling environment.


Pigment is a flexible modeling platform for teams willing to build and maintain their own planning models. Your team or an implementation partner designs it and keeps it running, so confirm who will own the model after go-live. It has a modern interface and supports scenario planning with visual modeling tools.


### 8. Vena


**Best for:** Teams that want to keep Excel as the front end while adding a central database, workflow automation and audit controls.


Vena keeps Excel as its front end and adds a centralized database, workflow automation and audit controls on the back end. It supports budgeting, forecasting and close, and integrations bring actuals into the central data layer. If AI-generated narrative or flexible dimensional analysis is a priority, weigh whether an Excel-native approach gives your team enough range.

## How to choose the right EPM platform


1.


**Rank the four jobs.** Which of budgeting, planning, control and allocation hurts most today? Weight your evaluation to match.


2.


**Test with a real plan.** Ask each vendor to show your approval flow and an allocation rule end to end.


3.


**Probe the AI.** Ask what the AI can change by itself. The safe pattern is that AI proposes, the calculation engine performs every calculation, and a person approves.


4.


**Confirm ownership.** If every change needs a consultant or specialist admin, your plan will lag the business.


5.


**Check the connections.** Confirm that your ERP and the data you need are covered.


## EPM software vs. spreadsheets: when to switch


Spreadsheets are flexible, and good finance teams use them well. The signs that you have outgrown them:


-


Several versions of the plan circulate and nobody is sure which is final.


-


Budget owners can't see or submit their own numbers without emailing a file.


-


Allocation rules are pasted values that nobody dares to touch.


-


Variance explanations take longer than the analysis.


-


It is hard to show an auditor who changed what.
